channel.title: People | CODAC
channel.description: The people of the DIGICAMS center, spanning control, optimization, cyber-physical systems, and applied category theory.

item.title: Cristian Nino
item.description: PhD in Mechanical Engineering under Warren Dixon; multi-agent tracking and coordination. Now a senior autonomous systems engineer at MITRE.

item.title: James Fairbanks
item.description: Assistant professor of Mechanical and Aerospace Engineering at the University of Florida; director and principal investigator of the DIGICAMS center.

item.title: Tyler Hanks
item.description: PhD on coordination sheaves; optimization, control and machine learning. Now on the faculty of the Florida Institute of Technology.

item.title: Warren Dixon
item.description: Dean of the Virginia Tech College of Engineering; lead of the learning and control thrust.

item.title: Brandon Fallin
item.description: PhD student in Mechanical Engineering under Warren Dixon; privacy and obfuscation for nonlinear control systems.

item.title: Matthew Hale
item.description: Associate professor of Electrical and Computer Engineering at Georgia Tech and director of the CORE Lab; lead of the compositional optimization thrust.

item.title: George Rauta
item.description: PhD student in CISE advised by James Fairbanks; numerical linear algebra and high-performance computing. Leads the Decapodes project.

item.title: Miroslav Pajic
item.description: Professor of Electrical and Computer Engineering at Duke University; lead of the decisions-under-uncertainty thrust.

item.title: Keith Currier
item.description: PhD student in Mechanical Engineering under Warren Dixon; physics-informed networks for nonlinear control, manifold learning, and network systems.

item.title: Kristopher Brown
item.description: Research scientist at the Topos Institute; lead of the implementation and deployment thrust.

item.title: David Spivak
item.description: Senior scientist at the Topos Institute; computational sheaf theory and decisions under uncertainty.

item.title: Joana Bou Barcelo
item.description: PhD student in Mechanical and Aerospace Engineering advised by James Fairbanks; cellular sheaves for multi-agent control.

item.title: Hans Riess
item.description: Research scientist in Electrical and Computer Engineering at Georgia Tech; computational and cellular sheaf theory.

item.title: Itay Kadosh
item.description: PhD student in Mechanical and Aerospace Engineering advised by James Fairbanks; distributed coordination for multi-agent systems.

item.title: Wilmer Leal
item.description: Research scientist in the Nonlinear Controls and Robotics lab; applied category theory, computational sheaf theory, and dynamical systems.

item.title: Richard Samuelson
item.description: Research scientist in the GATAS Lab; category theory, convex analysis, and high-performance computing.
